Definition: {to kneel; by implication to bless God (as an act of adoration), and (vice-versa) man (as a benefit); also (by euphemism) to curse (God or the king, as treason)}
BiblicalUsage: berak covers to bless, and it appears 5 times across the Bible. Daniel blesses the God of heaven when the mystery is revealed, and Nebuchadnezzar blesses the Most High when his reason returns.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that blessing God is the right answer to answered prayer, and Daniel's blessing after the mystery shows me how to respond. That is why I keep coming back to it: berak is not a word to rush past.
